etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin speciēs (“appearance; quality”), from speciō (“see”) + -iēs suffix signifying abstract noun. Doublet of spice.

definitions.definition: A group of plants or animals in which any two individuals of the appropriate sexes or mating types can produce fertile offspring, typically by sexual reproduction, usually having similar appearance.

quote.citation: 1834, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter IX, in Francesca Carrara. […], volume II, London: Richard Bentley, […], (successor to Henry Colburn), →OCLC, page 103:
quote.text: Louise felt raised above her species; a voice had spoken within her inmost soul, whose revealings were vouchsafed but to the chosen few; and what had been indifference, was now disdain.

quote.citation: 2012 January, Donald Worster, “A Drier and Hotter Future”, in American Scientist, volume 100, number 1, page 70:
quote.text: We may see many such [dust] storms in the decades ahead, along with species extinctions, radical disturbance of ecosystems, and intensified social conflict over land and water.

quote.citation: 2012, BioWare, Mass Effect 3 (Science Fiction), Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →OCLC, PC, scene: War Assets: Khalisah Bint Sinan al-Jilani:
quote.text: Westerlund News Reporter Khalisah Bint Sinan al-Jilani reached out recently to her viewers with a wartime plea for unity and cooperation among all galactic species.UPDATEDHer sincerity touched extranet viewers and donations for war relief efforts are pouring in, both to the Alliance and its alien allies.

definitions.definition: (biology, taxonomy) A category in the classification of organisms, ranking below genus; a taxon at that rank.

quote.citation: 1859 November 24, Charles Darwin, “Variation under Nature”, in On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, […], London: John Murray, […], →OCLC, page 47:
quote.text: Hence, in determining whether a form should be ranked as a species or a variety, the opinion of naturalists having sound judgment and wide experience seems the only guide to follow.

quote.citation: 1992, Rudolf M[athias] Schuster, The Hepaticae and Anthocerotae of North America: East of the Hundredth Meridian, volume V, Chicago, Ill.: Field Museum of Natural History, →ISBN, page vii:
quote.text: Firstly, I continue to base most species treatments on personally collected material, rather than on herbarium plants.

quote.citation: 2013 May-June, David Van Tassel, Lee DeHaan, “Wild Plants to the Rescue”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 3:
quote.text: Plant breeding is always a numbers game. […] The wild species we use are rich in genetic variation, and individual plants are highly heterozygous and do not breed true. In addition, we are looking for rare alleles, so the more plants we try, the better.

definitions.definition: (chemistry, physics) A particular type of atom, molecule, ion or other particle.
(mineralogy) A mineral with a unique chemical formula whose crystals belong to a unique crystallographic system.

quote.citation: 1871, Richard Holt Hutton, Essays, Theological and Literary:
quote.text: What is called spiritualism should, I think, be called a mental species of materialism.

quote.citation: 1930, Norman Lindsay, Redheap, Sydney, N.S.W.: Ure Smith, published 1965, →OCLC, page 122:
quote.text: He went on kissing her with unflagging industry, while she remained limply in his arms, in a species of satisfied trance.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) The image of something cast on a surface, or reflected from a surface, or refracted through a lens or telescope; a reflection.
Visible or perceptible presentation; appearance; something perceived.

quote.citation: 1667, John Dryden, Annus Mirabilis: The Year of Wonders, 1666. […], London:  […]  Henry Herringman, […], →OCLC, (please specify the stanza number):
quote.text: Wit, […] the faculty of imagination in the writer, which searches over all the memory for the species or ideas of those things which it designs to represent.

quote.citation: 1704, I[saac] N[ewton], “(please specify |book=1 to 3)”, in Opticks: Or, A Treatise of the Reflexions, Refractions, Inflexions and Colours of Light. […], London:  […]  Sam[uel] Smith, and Benj[amin] Walford, printers to the Royal Society, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: the species of the letters illuminated with indigo and violet

definitions.definition: An image, an appearance, a spectacle.
(Christianity) Either of the two elements of the Eucharist after they have been consecrated.
Coin, or coined silver, gold, or other metal, used as a circulating medium; specie.

quote.citation: 1727, John Arbuthnot, Tables of Ancient Coins, Weights and Measures:
quote.text: There was, in the splendour of the Roman empire, a less quantity of current species in Europe than there is now.

definitions.definition: A component part of compound medicine; a simple.
